newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Metals outlook weighs on Australian major miners.
newsitem.headline: Metals outlook weighs on Australian major miners.

text.p: Shares in the leading miners led the way lower in the Australian share market on Friday with the big three all feeling the pressure from a cloudy outlook for commodities.
Bellwether and major copper producer BHP shed 1.6 percent to A$17.95, global mining giant Rio Tinto lost 1.1 percent to A$20.65, while gold and nickel producer WMC was down 1.6 percent at A$7.66.
Brokers said while most base metals had firmed marginally in offshore trade, the activity in most metals markets remained volatile with investors needing more evidence before buying.
"People are still waiting for some more positive evidence that they should be hopping into the resources," said head of institutions at Ord Minnett, Eric Gale.
This sentiment was shared by others, who noted the ongoing gyrations in the metals markets.
"There were generally better prices last night but there is still some uncertainty about future direction," said Henderson Charlton Jones dealer, Phillip Toop.
"There has been nothing in particular today but people seem a little bit more pessimistic," he added.

By 12.10 p.m. (0210 GMT), BHP shares were 27 cents or 1.5 percent lower at A$17.97, Rio Tinto shares were 18.7 cents down at A$20.69, while WMC shares were 1.4 percent lower at A$7.68, all in only moderate volumes.
